definitions.explanation: The act of adjusting something again, whether schedules, plans, equipment, or policies.

examples.japanese: スケジュールの{再調整|さいちょうせい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: We need to readjust the schedule.

examples.japanese: {予算|よさん}の{再調整|さいちょうせい}を{行|おこな}うことになった。
examples.english: It was decided to readjust the budget.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいデータに{基|もと}づいて{計画|けいかく}の{再調整|さいちょうせい}を{進|すす}めているが、{関係者|かんけいしゃ}との{合意|ごうい}にはまだ{時間|じかん}がかかりそうだ。
examples.english: We are proceeding with readjusting the plan based on new data, but reaching consensus with stakeholders will likely take more time.

notes:
Composed of {再|さい} (re-, again) + {調整|ちょうせい} (adjustment, coordination). A productive compound that appears frequently in business, project management, and technical contexts. Can be used as a noun or with する as a verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {再調整|さいちょうせい}する — to readjust
- スケジュールの{再調整|さいちょうせい} — schedule readjustment
- {予算|よさん}の{再調整|さいちょうせい} — budget readjustment
- {方針|ほうしん}の{再調整|さいちょうせい} — policy readjustment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {調整|ちょうせい} — adjustment, coordination; the base form without the "re-" prefix
- {見直|みなお}し — review, reassessment; focuses on re-examining rather than re-adjusting
- {修正|しゅうせい} — correction, revision; implies fixing errors rather than making new adjustments
